title: A continuous representation of a profinite group stabilizes a lattice
statement: Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $G$ be a compact topological group (for instance a profinite group), let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space with its $\ell$-adic topology (the product topology for any basis), and let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ be a homomorphism such that $G\times V\to V$, $(g,v)\mapsto\rho(g)v$, is continuous. Then there is an $\mathcal O_E$-lattice $\Lambda\subset V$ (a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-submodule spanning $V$ over $E$, necessarily free of rank $\dim_EV$) with $\rho(g)\Lambda=\Lambda$ for all $g\in G$; and $G\times\Lambda\to\Lambda$ is continuous for the $\mathfrak m_E$-adic topology of $\Lambda$, which is the subspace topology from $V$.

source.place: Stanford Weil II seminar, lecture 19 (notes by D. Dore), Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, pp. 2-3: 'for any lattice Lambda_0, GL(Lambda_0) is an open subgroup [of GL_n(E)], so its stabilizer has finite index in the profinite group pi_1; then by adding the finitely many translates of Lambda_0 we get a new lattice Lambda which is stable'

proof.text: Choose an E-basis of V and let Lambda_0 be its O_E-span. This is an O_E-lattice. By lem-pod-lattice-stabilizer-open, its stabilizer U in GL_E(V) is open. In the chosen basis, the matrix entries of rho(g) are obtained by evaluating the continuous action map on basis vectors, so rho is continuous for the compact-open topology on linear maps; hence H=rho^{-1}(U) is an open subgroup of G.
The compact group G is covered by the open cosets gH. A finite subcover gives representatives g_1,...,g_r with G=\bigcup_i g_iH.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2: the stabilizer has finite index in the profinite group

proof.text: Set Lambda=\sum_i rho(g_i)Lambda_0. It is finitely generated and contains Lambda_0, so it spans V over E. It is torsion-free because it is a submodule of the E-vector space V. Since O_E is a discrete valuation ring, the existing Mathlib leaf lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free gives that Lambda is finite free, hence an O_E-lattice. For g\in G and each i, write gg_i=g_jh with h\in H; then rho(g)rho(g_i)Lambda_0=rho(g_j)rho(h)Lambda_0=rho(g_j)Lambda_0, so rho(g)Lambda\subseteq Lambda. Applying the same inclusion to g^{-1} gives equality.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, pp. 2-3: add the finitely many translates of Lambda_0

proof.text: The action map G\times Lambda\to Lambda is continuous because it is the restriction of the given continuous map G\times V\to V to the subspace Lambda, and its image lies in Lambda by stability. Choose an O_E-basis of Lambda. Then Lambda is identified with O_E^r inside E^r, and the sets varpi_E^n O_E^r form both the m_E-adic neighborhood basis and the subspace neighborhood basis; therefore the two topologies agree.
